name: Dermal Fillers
summary: Hyaluronic-acid injectable fillers used to add volume and support facial contour.
leadAnswer: Dermal fillers are hyaluronic-acid (HA) based injectables used by a doctor to add volume or support the shape of specific facial areas. At Kaiteki these include Juvederm, Restylane, Belotero and Art Filler. Filler is placed into the face by a doctor, so facial structure and your medical history are assessed before any product, plane or plan is chosen.

sessionSteps.title: Consultation and facial assessment
sessionSteps.body: Your first visit is a consultation, not a treatment. The doctor assesses your facial proportions and medical history, decides which areas to address and in what order, and explains the risks before you consent.

sessionSteps.title: Product and preparation
sessionSteps.body: After a facial assessment, the doctor selects a product for the area, cleanses the skin and, where relevant, applies topical numbing before injecting.

sessionSteps.title: The injections
sessionSteps.body: The gel is placed in small increments with a needle or a cannula. A single area often takes 15 to 30 minutes once preparation is done, and many plans are staged across more than one visit.

sessionSteps.title: Review
sessionSteps.body: A review appointment is commonly arranged so the doctor can assess the area once the swelling has settled.

afterSession.intro: Mild swelling, redness, bruising or tenderness at the injection sites commonly settles within a few days to about a week. Follow the aftercare you are given, which may include avoiding certain activities for a few days, and contact the clinic with any concern.

bands.title: The first few days
bands.body: The lips and under-eye area tend to swell more visibly than the cheeks or jawline. Allow a comfortable margin before any event that matters to you.

afterSession.aftercare: Avoid pressure or massage on the treated site, keep strenuous exercise, heat and alcohol to a minimum for a short period, and contact the clinic promptly if anything feels unusual.

risks.intro: Filler is an injectable medical device, and its risks are explained at consultation before you consent.
risks.common: Common temporary effects are swelling, redness, bruising, tenderness or lumpiness at the injection site, which typically settle.
risks.lessCommon: Infection, inflammatory nodules and delayed hypersensitivity. The most serious recognised risk of any filler is vascular occlusion: filler entering or compressing a blood vessel, which can affect the skin or, rarely, vision.
cannotDo: It is not permanent: hyaluronic-acid filler is gradually broken down by the body.
It does not relax muscle, so it does not address lines caused by movement.
Dissolving it is not a routine undo. Hyaluronidase is a medical procedure with its own risks, and not appropriate in every situation.
risks.disclose: Report sudden pain, skin blanching or any change in vision to the clinic immediately, rather than waiting.

sections.heading: What are dermal fillers?
body: Dermal fillers are injectable gels based on hyaluronic acid (HA), a substance naturally present in skin. They are formulated to sit within the tissue and provide volume or support directly once injected.
At Kaiteki the ranges are Juvederm, Restylane, Belotero and Art Filler (Laboratoires Fillmed).

Fillers are commonly considered for volume loss in the cheeks or temples, definition of the chin, jawline or nose bridge, static lines such as nasolabial folds and marionette lines, and lip volume and shape.

sections.heading: How does a hyaluronic acid gel add volume?
body: HA fillers are injected into targeted layers of the skin or the tissue beneath it, where the gel is intended to provide volume or structural support at the treated site.

Formulations differ in thickness and in how they behave in tissue, which is why the doctor matches the product and technique to the area. The effect is present from injection and continues to settle over the following days.

faqs.q: What is the difference between dermal fillers and bio-stimulators?
faqs.a: Dermal fillers are HA gels that provide volume or support once injected. Bio-stimulators work gradually, by supporting the skin's own structural renewal.

faqs.q: How long do dermal fillers last?
faqs.a: It depends on the product, the area treated and how your body breaks it down. The doctor can say what is realistic for the filler and area being considered.
Some HA fillers can, in certain circumstances, be broken down with a dissolving agent. Whether that applies to your product and situation is assessed individually.

Most people describe filler injection as briefly uncomfortable rather than painful. Topical numbing may be applied first, and many filler gels contain lidocaine. Lips are generally more sensitive than cheeks.

faqs.q: Are dermal fillers safe for Asian skin?
faqs.a: Hyaluronic-acid fillers do not use light or heat, so skin tone is not the limiting factor it can be with lasers. Facial anatomy and medical history matter far more, and the doctor assesses both before deciding whether filler is appropriate.

faqs.q: What are the warning signs after filler?
faqs.a: Sudden pain, skin blanching or any change in vision can signal filler affecting a blood vessel, the most serious recognised risk of any filler. Contact the clinic immediately rather than waiting.
